record.field: Used for: Explosives (Divisions 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.4, 1.5, 1.6), Self-reactive substances and mixtures (Types A and B), Organic peroxides (Types A and B), Desensitised explosives (Category 1).

Used for: Flammable gases, Aerosols (Categories 1 and 2), Flammable liquids, Flammable solids, Self-reactive substances (Types B–F), Pyrophoric liquids and solids, Self-heating substances, Substances which emit flammable gas on contact with water, Organic peroxides (Types B–F), Desensitised explosives (Categories 2, 3, 4).
Used for: Oxidising gases (Category 1), Oxidising liquids (Categories 1, 2, 3), Oxidising solids (Categories 1, 2, 3).
Used for: Gases under pressure — Compressed gases, Liquefied gases, Refrigerated liquefied gases, Dissolved gases.
Used for: Corrosive to metals (Category 1), Skin corrosion (Categories 1A, 1B, 1C), Serious eye damage (Category 1).
Used for: Acute toxicity (oral, dermal, inhalation) — Categories 1, 2 and 3 (fatal or toxic).

Used for: Acute toxicity (Category 4 — harmful), Skin irritation (Category 2), Eye irritation (Category 2), Skin sensitisation (Category 1), Specific target organ toxicity — single exposure (Category 3), Respiratory tract irritation, Narcotic effects, Hazardous to the ozone layer.

Used for: Respiratory sensitisation (Category 1), Germ cell mutagenicity (Categories 1A, 1B, 2), Carcinogenicity (Categories 1A, 1B, 2), Reproductive toxicity (Categories 1A, 1B, 2), Specific target organ toxicity — single exposure (Categories 1, 2), Specific target organ toxicity — repeated exposure (Categories 1, 2), Aspiration hazard (Categories 1, 2).
Used for: Hazardous to the aquatic environment — Acute hazard (Category 1), Chronic hazard (Categories 1 and 2). Note: use of this pictogram is mandatory in Australia for the listed categories.
